Jono Kruger Unsung Hero

By: Tarryn Crossman | Paid

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
He was a just a small town guy who as he put it, went behind the invisible curtain of poverty and could never unsee what he saw.

In grade 10, a teacher took Jono’s team to Duncan village, a nearby township, to do a clean-up and help the community.
Since that day, Jono’s life purpose has been to make an impact.

People often say that runners are running away from something, but Jono is running towards something. He runs to change the lives of destitute children in the Eastern Cape.
He was born in EL, raised in EL, and is still here to serve the people.

After school Jono played professional rugby. It was here that he started trying to use sports to change lives. He teamed up with his team mate – Tiger – and together they started a small NGO, Champions development. They put their feet on the ground and went from school to school teaching basic rugby skills and offering life guidance.

It really all exploded though when he was working as a teacher at his old school, Selbourne collage, he was coaching rugby and realised that most of the kids who came from super privileged backgrounds had idea what was going on in their own country.
He was determined to make them play for more than just the glory, so he took the boys to a local orphanage for the day, and then told them that the rest of their season would be dedicated to these kids.
At the end of that year the team had raised nearly 100k for the orphanage. It was a life changer for many of the boys, who to this day talk about how that year and experience has impacted the way they live now.

And so SPORT FOR LIVES was born. An online platform where athletes around South Africa can start a campaign to raise funds for an NGO of their choice. Playing for more than the glory, today the platform has raised over 2 million rand.

Even though the platform was a success, Jono still had a day job as a teacher and wasn't able to really live out his passion to create change.
BUT After our story on Jono and what Sport for lives was achieving broadcast it all changed.
A guardian angel appeared in the form of a local businessman who basically said, what do you really want to do, and how much do you need to do it

Jono left teaching and started Edusports, today they have 30 sports coaches and literacy leaders going into 5 schools every day. They have a sports field, a rec room and a campsite for sports and life skills camp. Jono has a 5 year plan for Edusports that will see them coaching sports teams that will compete nationally. And single handily changing children’s lives by teaching them how to read and write

Jono says – “so many South Africans are immigrating to give their children a better life, but I don’t want to teach my children that it’s all about them having the best of the best. Their lives should be about making a difference. I believe South Africa needs all of us to pay it forward. How can I turn a blind eye to this? “


This is the story of a professional athlete, who believed there was more to play for than the glory. It's the story of a South African that won't look away, and instead has dedicated his life to making it better, for the next generation.

JONO - a business approached me, they said to me,
What if we took care of you and looked after your needs and set you free to just run with your passion?

Finishing the run

Masa and jono
a lot of people say, oh, this place is going to the dogs, and especially people with young children. They worry about safety and they prefer to immigrate for the sake of their children.
